newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil weaker.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Monday, with gas oil softer and high sulphur cracked fuel steady, traders said.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were seen steady but activity was sapped by pre-Christmas lethargy. An Italian refiner sold a small January-loading cargo containing three percent sulphur to an end user at a p+c premium to the high fob of published quotes, traders said. But activity was otherwise thin, with continued support seen from Romania.
Low sulphur markets were slightly weaker as crude oil futures slipped lower. Swaps traded at $125.50 fob NWE.

Gasoline and naphtha levels were pegged around $3 a tonne below Friday's levels but most levels were notional with few traders at their desks. Naphtha held around a $3-4 a tonne premium to gasoline and traders saw the market as reasonably balanced though some pointed to quiet availablility.
"There's material there but as the buyers are not the sellers are keeping it quiet. Prices will have to come down," one trader said.
Gas oil slipped $3.50 a tonne in line with futures. The cash market was also weak in thin, holiday-affected trade.
Heating oil premiums remained around high cif quotes flat to +$0.50 basis Genoa.

The market continues quiet and balanced, with two Russian heating oil cargoes on offer and a one percent sulphur heating oil cargo available from Lavera. Traders see more demand towards the end of December as January requirements emerge.

Traders said most attention centred on attempts to work an arb to Singapore and other eastern destinations but added a rise in freight rates by some 30 percent from last week continued to complicate efforts to charter vessels to move material to Asia.
